passage:
In the back of Sunny Café, there is a wall full of postcards. Customers can write a postcard to anyone and leave it with the owner. Every Monday, the owner mails them.
Some postcards travel across the country. Others go only a few streets away. Many are simple messages: "Thank you for helping me," "I miss you," or "Good luck on your test."
One day, a student named Iris wrote a postcard to herself. She wrote, "You are doing better than you think." A week later, she received it at home and smiled.
The postcard wall became popular because writing by hand feels different from sending a quick message. A postcard moves slowly, but sometimes slow words arrive more deeply.
